quests.passage: A good title makes a promise and keeps it. It tells the reader roughly what to expect, without giving away everything, and it fits the text that follows. Titles fail in two opposite ways: too broad, they promise more than the text delivers; too narrow, they draw attention to one detail and ignore the rest. Editors often write the title last, when they know what the piece is really about.
